🚨 Apache Roller is being actively exploited through a critical unauthenticated deserialization flaw; CVE-2026-129448

PoC: https://github.com/Yanixos/APACHE-CVE-2026-129448

The vulnerability affects Roller’s XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authenticating the requester. An unauthenticated remote attacker can abuse this behavior to execute arbitrary code.

Apache Roller | Unauthenticated RCE:

• CVSS: 9.8 Critical
• Attack: Remote, unauthenticated
• Affected: Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4
• Fixed: Upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later
• Impact: Arbitrary code execution
• Status: Actively exploited in the wild

The issue is the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which previously listed a much narrower affected-version range.

Apache recommends upgrading immediately or disabling extension types and removing the vulnerable XML-RPC servlet mapping if an upgrade cannot be performed yet.

CVE-2026-82384.description: Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller 6.1.5 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes, because the XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types that are deserialized during request parsing, before authentication. The servlet is mapped unconditionally, so parsing occurs even when the global XML-RPC feature is set to disabled; no non-default configuration is required for this path. This can lead to remote code execution. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

🚨 Apache Roller is being actively exploited through a critical unauthenticated deserialization flaw; CVE-2026-129448

PoC: https://github.com/Yanixos/APACHE-CVE-2026-129448

The vulnerability affects Roller’s XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authenticating the requester. An unauthenticated remote attacker can abuse this behavior to execute arbitrary code.

Apache Roller | Unauthenticated RCE:

• CVSS: 9.8 Critical
• Attack: Remote, unauthenticated
• Affected: Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4
• Fixed: Upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later
• Impact: Arbitrary code execution
• Status: Actively exploited in the wild

The issue is the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which previously listed a much narrower affected-version range.

Apache recommends upgrading immediately or disabling extension types and removing the vulnerable XML-RPC servlet mapping if an upgrade cannot be performed yet.

CVE-2026-129448.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

CVE-2026-129223.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE-2026-22308.description:
The preview mode of the OPC (OnPage Composer) page
builder of JTL-Shop is activated by a request parameter alone and
renders page data supplied in the request without checking for an authenticated
backend session with the corresponding permission. Several portlet properties
are output without output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker
can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a
visitor or administrator who opens a crafted link; in the case of an
administrator, actions can be performed with the administrator's privileges. Third-party
plugins whose portlets evaluate property values as templates can
additionally be made to execute template code through the same entry point. This is
a separate flaw in such plugins and does not affect the portlets of JTL-Shop itself.

CVE-2026-123007.description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

🚨 BREAKING: A NEW CRITICAL PHP VULNERABILITY COULD LET HACKERS EXECUTE CODE ON WEB SERVERS WITHOUT LOGGING IN.

Dubbed phpAfterShell, CVE-2026-126714 carries a CVSS score of 9.2 and affects PHP's default file-based session handler.

Security researchers at depthfirst discovered that interrupting a PHP session write can leave behind a corrupted session file containing attacker-controlled data. When PHP loads that session again, a suitable exploit chain can turn the corruption into remote code execution.

The concerning part? Researchers demonstrated an attack path that begins while PHP is processing an unauthenticated file upload, before the application's PHP script even starts running. Exploitation still requires specific conditions, including a suitable deserialization chain.

PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 are affected. Security fixes are now available in versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-126714.description:
Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-129289.description:
PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.



Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.



This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-129496.description:
Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-129481.description:
Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.

The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
